text_blocks.snippet: Residents in Central Illinois face frequent threats from digital, phone, and in-person cons, highlighted by fake toll/traffic violation text messages, phony delivery notifications, and seasonal online shopping traps. Government agencies and local watchdogs urge the public to recognize these prominent local schemes.

list.snippet: Fake Toll and Traffic Texts: Scammers send texts claiming you owe unpaid toll or traffic fines, threatening license suspension or extra fees if you do not click a link.
Package Delivery Smishing: Fraudulent texts pretend to be from the USPS, UPS, or other carriers, stating a package cannot be delivered unless you verify your address or pay a small fee.
Online Shopping and Holiday Ads: Fake social media ads and polished websites offer popular electronics, toys, or holiday gifts at steep discounts to steal credit card data.
Government and Tax Impersonation: Con artists text or call pretending to be the Illinois Department of Revenue, court officials, or police, demanding immediate payment via untraceable methods.
Emergency and Home Repair Scams: Transient contractors target neighborhoods after severe weather, demanding large cash deposits upfront without proper local licensing.
Do not click links in unexpected text messages or emails regarding fines, tolls, or package deliveries.

Practice the pause
by stopping to independently verify urgent or secretive requests for money or personal data.
Verify websites by checking the URL and looking for clear return policies before making online purchases.

Never pay via gift cards

, wire transfers, or cryptocurrency.

Report suspicious activity to the Better Business Bureau of Central Illinois or file a complaint with the Illinois Attorney General

.
